# Hatcher — Algebraic Topology (2002)

[Source index](../../../README.md) · [Reading entrance](../../../../../../README.md) · [48 movements](../../../../../../section-rooms/README.md)

## Chicago 18 forms

**Full note:** Allen Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology* (Cambridge University Press, 2002), {page/example/proposition}, https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATpage.html.

**Shortened note:** Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, {page}.

**Bibliography:** Hatcher, Allen. *Algebraic Topology*. Cambridge University Press, 2002. https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATpage.html.

## Essay use

Standard mathematical reference for quotient constructions, covering spaces, the torus, fundamental groups, and the relation `T² = R²/Z²`. It secures the exact topology beneath the toroidal image.

**Located operations:** the torus cell presentation (p. 5); the product fundamental group (p. 34); path lifting (pp. 60–61); integer-translation and Klein-bottle quotient actions (p. 74). The sphere comparison is located at Proposition 1.14, p. 35. These are selected passages, not a complete surface-classification survey.

**Claim boundary:** Hatcher warrants the extracted facts of quotient, covering, cycle, and winding. Their coordination as the arche-topos is the essay's argued QL interpretation and bears its own proof burden.

<a id="hatcher-2002-algebraic-topology-p001"></a>
## Passage card — `hatcher-2002-algebraic-topology-p001` — Torus cell presentation and independent generators

Opposite sides of a square are identified in pairs, yielding one vertex, two edges and one face. The product rule gives the torus fundamental group as two independent integer windings.

- **Locator:** “Cell Complexes,” p. 5 (PDF 14); Proposition 1.12 and Example 1.13, p. 34 (PDF 43).
- **Status:** paraphrase-only.
- **Verification:** assistant, 2026-09-29; author-hosted corrected PDF, text and screenshot inspection; no OCR.
- **Source relation:** extracted.
- **Evidential action:** supports.
- **Consumers:** [[section-rooms/arguments/A17-Toroidal-Circulation-and-the-Arche-Topos|Toroidal Circulation and the Arche-Topos]].
- **Use boundary:** four polygon sides before identification are not four quotient vertices.

<a id="hatcher-2002-algebraic-topology-p002"></a>
## Passage card — `hatcher-2002-algebraic-topology-p002` — Chosen lifts and closed loops

A path lifts uniquely after a starting lift is chosen. Which loops lift to loops depends on the covering subgroup. A homotopy class retains less information than a parametrised path.

- **Locator:** Proposition 1.30 and ensuing path-lifting discussion, p. 60 (PDF 69); Propositions 1.31–1.32, p. 61 (PDF 70).
- **Status:** paraphrase-only.
- **Verification:** assistant, 2026-09-29; author-hosted corrected PDF, text and screenshot inspection; no OCR.
- **Source relation:** extracted; the worked torus endpoint comparison is developed in the consumer.
- **Evidential action:** qualifies.
- **Consumers:** [[section-rooms/arguments/A17-Toroidal-Circulation-and-the-Arche-Topos|Toroidal Circulation and the Arche-Topos]].
- **Use boundary:** an endpoint displacement does not reconstruct every turn or timing of a travelled path.

<a id="hatcher-2002-algebraic-topology-p003"></a>
## Passage card — `hatcher-2002-algebraic-topology-p003` — Different quotient groups, different covers

Integer translations of the plane give a torus quotient. The Klein-bottle action includes a glide-reflection; its index-two translation subgroup gives a torus double cover. These are different covering maps.

- **Locator:** Example 1.42, p. 74 (PDF 83); compare Example 1.46, p. 77 (PDF 86).
- **Status:** paraphrase-only.
- **Verification:** assistant, 2026-09-29; author-hosted corrected PDF, diagrams and text inspected together; no OCR.
- **Source relation:** extracted.
- **Evidential action:** supports and distinguishes.
- **Consumers:** [[section-rooms/arguments/A17-Toroidal-Circulation-and-the-Arche-Topos|Toroidal Circulation and the Arche-Topos]].
- **Use boundary:** the plane-to-torus map has infinite fibres; the torus-to-Klein-bottle map has two-point fibres.

<a id="hatcher-2002-algebraic-topology-p004"></a>
## Passage card — `hatcher-2002-algebraic-topology-p004` — The sphere comparison

For spheres of dimension at least two, the fundamental group is trivial. Thus a sphere has no non-contractible loop class; this does not prohibit paths or physical motion on it.

- **Locator:** Proposition 1.14 and its proof, p. 35 (PDF 44).
- **Status:** paraphrase-only.
- **Verification:** assistant, 2026-09-29; author-hosted corrected PDF, text and screenshot inspection; no OCR.
- **Source relation:** extracted; the distinction from physical motion states the consumer's scope.
- **Evidential action:** qualifies.
- **Consumers:** [[section-rooms/arguments/A17-Toroidal-Circulation-and-the-Arche-Topos|Toroidal Circulation and the Arche-Topos]].
- **Use boundary:** no physical conservation or optimality theorem follows from simply connectedness.
